title: Three-Week IB Mandarin B Revision Plan for November
summary: IB Mandarin B revision plan for November: triage themes, strengthen every skill, protect rest and enter exams prepared with greater confidence.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before an IB examination session can feel strangely short. There is enough time to improve, but not enough time to revise everything equally. That distinction matters.


A strong **IB Mandarin B revision plan** should therefore do three things: identify where marks are being lost, concentrate practice on those weaknesses, and preserve enough energy for your other subjects. For most students, that means using week one to diagnose, week two to improve, and week three to rehearse under timed conditions.


This plan covers Paper 1 writing and Paper 2 listening and reading. It is deliberately flexible. A student with several November subjects can follow the minimum schedule, while someone with more available time can add the optional sessions.


### Your three-week overview


Week Main priority Mandarin workload


Week one Diagnose weaknesses and triage themes 5 focused sessions of 30-50 minutes


Week two Repair recurring problems through targeted practice 5-6 sessions, including one timed section


Week three Rehearse exam conditions and reduce intensity 4-5 sessions, including timed papers


Keep one evening each week completely free from Mandarin. Rest is not time stolen from revision. It is part of the system that lets you remember what you studied.


### Before week one: build an honest starting point


The official Language B structure assesses productive writing in Paper 1 and receptive listening and reading in Paper 2. The course is organised around five themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation, and sharing the planet. RevisionDojo’s guide to the[five core themes of IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/the-five-core-themes-of-ib-chinese-b-explained) can help you review their scope.


Before planning individual days, take one short writing task, one reading passage, and one listening exercise without notes. Do not treat the result as a prediction. Treat it as a map.


Sort each weakness into one of four categories:


- **Language:** limited vocabulary, inaccurate characters, grammar or connectors
- **Comprehension:** missing details, inference or speaker intention
- **Task control:** misunderstanding purpose, audience or required text type
- **Timing:** knowing what to do but working too slowly


This distinction prevents vague revision. “Improve Mandarin” is impossible to schedule. “Practise selecting evidence from reading texts” fits into Tuesday afternoon.


### Week one: diagnose and triage


The first week is about discovering which improvements are realistic. Begin with your weakest two skills, not your favourite two.


### Days one and two: assess writing and reading


On day one, complete a Paper 1 task with a comfortable time limit. Afterwards, highlight where you addressed the audience, purpose and context. Check whether the text type is recognisable without reading the prompt. Then make a short correction list containing no more than five recurring problems.


On day two, complete a reading set. For every incorrect answer, label the cause: unknown word, overlooked evidence, inference error or rushed decision. The[IB Chinese B grading guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-chinese-b-grading-explained-what-students-need-to-know) provides useful context for deciding where your effort matters.


### Days three and four: assess listening and themes


For listening, resist the temptation to replay every difficult sentence immediately. First attempt the complete exercise under realistic conditions. On the second listen, note signal words, contrasts, numbers, opinions and changes of speaker.


If listening is your weakest area, use the strategies in[How to Improve Listening in IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-improve-listening-in-ib-chinese-b) . A productive correction routine is to replay a short section, transcribe what you hear, compare it with the available transcript or answer guidance, and record only the vocabulary that affected comprehension.


Next, score each prescribed theme from one to three:


- **One:** vocabulary gaps prevent you discussing common questions
- **Two:** you can communicate, but ideas or examples are repetitive
- **Three:** you can explain, compare and justify views with relevant vocabulary


Spend the final session of week one building Flashcards for themes scored one. Avoid copying enormous word lists. Choose transferable language for causes, consequences, comparisons, solutions and personal viewpoints.


A student calmly takes a tea break while an intimidating calendar announces its deadlines.


### Week two: turn weaknesses into routines


Week two should feel less broad. You have identified the leaks; now you repair them one at a time.


A realistic weekday session might contain 10 minutes of Flashcards, 25 minutes of targeted questions, and 10 minutes of correction. On a busy day, complete only the targeted questions and record one lesson learned. Consistency matters more than constructing a perfect two-hour study block that never happens.


### Build Paper 1 control


Complete two writing tasks this week. The first can be untimed, with emphasis on planning and text conventions. The second should be timed according to the requirements your teacher has given you.


Before writing, spend a few minutes identifying:


- who is communicating
- who will read the text
- what response the prompt requires
- which text type best fits that situation
- which two or three ideas can be developed clearly


Do not memorise an entire model response. Memorised essays often become awkward when the prompt changes. Instead, build reusable components: openings, transitions, ways to introduce examples, balanced opinions and appropriate closings. RevisionDojo’s overview of[skills developed in IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-skills-does-ib-chinese-b-develop) helps connect language knowledge with productive and interactive communication.


Use Grading tools or a teacher to examine whether your response answers the task, not merely whether each sentence is grammatically possible. If the same mistake appears repeatedly, ask AI Chat to explain the underlying rule and generate a short contrast exercise. A Tutor can be especially useful when errors involve register, natural phrasing or text-type expectations.


### Train listening and reading separately


Listening and reading belong to the same receptive paper, but they do not always fail for the same reason. Alternate them across the week rather than combining both into one exhausting session.


In reading, practise locating evidence before interpreting unfamiliar vocabulary. In listening, preview questions carefully and predict the kind of information required. The guide to[Chinese B Paper 2 listening and reading](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-prepare-for-ib-chinese-b-paper-2-listening-and-reading) offers a focused routine for both components.


Use the[IB Questionbank and Exam Practice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) page to select questions matching the skill or theme you are repairing. Review every answer while the reasoning is still fresh. A completed question without a correction teaches less than a smaller set analysed properly.


### Week three: rehearse, review and taper


The final week is not the moment to double your workload. It is the moment to make familiar skills reliable under pressure.


Early in the week, sit a complete timed writing paper in Exam mode. On a separate day, complete a timed receptive paper. Use authorised examination materials supplied through your school or current RevisionDojo Predicted Papers and Mock Exams that match your level and syllabus.


After each attempt, create a one-page error log. Divide it into three columns: what happened, why it happened, and what you will do next time. The final column must describe an action. “Be careful” is not an action; “underline the audience before choosing a text type” is.


Students balancing several subjects can use this final-week pattern:


- **Six or more days remaining:** one timed paper or section
- **Four to five days remaining:** targeted correction from the error log
- **Two to three days remaining:** short vocabulary, listening and planning drills
- **Day before the examination:** 20-30 minutes of light review, then stop


The[Chinese B tips for non-native learners](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-chinese-b-tips-for-non-native-learners) are useful if confidence drops during this final stretch. Keep your sleep and meal routine stable. Do not sacrifice the next day’s concentration for a late session with diminishing returns.


### Use practice material without wasting it


Full examination sets are limited and valuable. Do not consume them simply to obtain another score. Early in the plan, break material into sections for diagnosis and repair. Save complete, unseen sets for week three, when timing and stamina become the priority.


Reviewing is where the learning happens. For reading and listening, locate the evidence supporting each answer. For writing, compare your choices with the assessment criteria and record patterns across multiple attempts. If a mistake appears once, notice it. If it appears three times, design a drill for it.


RevisionDojo works best here as a connected system. Study Notes and Flashcards rebuild knowledge, the Questionbank supplies focused practice, and AI Chat or Tutors help resolve confusion. Grading tools make feedback actionable, while Predicted Papers and Mock Exams test performance under pressure. The Coursework Library is less important if your coursework is already complete, so protect exam revision time rather than reopening finished work.


### Finish with a plan you can actually follow


Three weeks will not make every character, theme and text type equally comfortable. It can, however, make your decisions faster and your recurring mistakes less frequent.


The best plan is not the most ambitious one written on Sunday night. It is the one that survives a busy Tuesday, another subject’s examination, and an evening when concentration is low. Keep the minimum version small, add optional practice when energy allows, and preserve rest without guilt.


Begin by identifying one writing weakness and one receptive weakness. Then[practise targeted questions in the RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/questionbank) . When the final week arrives, sit timed papers in Exam mode so that November feels like a familiar routine rather than a first encounter.
